scope: Process-owned native file store integrated into the actual host factory and independently compiled native-authorization product fixture. Software-only PTY/simulated MCU evidence; standard restart, retained Moonraker listener/auth/database and physical machine acceptance are incomplete.
verified: One process file directory descriptor, lock and recovered catalog survive profile release and native reinitialization; final host shutdown releases them.
An exclusive generation lease rejects overlap and storage-root identity changes before adapter acquisition.
Old native file admission is closed; ignored cancellation drains before adapter retirement and lease transfer.
Partial metadata startup releases the lease without destroying process storage. Adapter retirement failure remains a rejected generation outcome.
The actual two-MCU PTY product host uploads, reinitializes, lists and downloads the same bytes, rejects old-generation access and stops each simulated device once.
Process factory cleanup executes after final profile retirement and on startup/retirement failures; errors remain observable.

An independently compiled JWT/API-load product journey uses the process factory, verifies the retained file lock in its second device generation and records exactly one process file close after profile retirement.

childRuntime.devices: PTY models owned by test parent; no physical machine

primary.scope: File generation acquisition/catalog/release on cached local storage. Cold initial process opens excluded from retained samples and reported separately. No motion or hardware performance claim.

fileOwnershipBenchmark.primaryRunConditions: Sequential run after all test/build handles completed. Cached local filesystem; both modes return the same 256-file catalog. Initial retained-store cold open is separately reported, not eliminated.

exploratory.scope: File generation acquisition/catalog/release on cached local storage. Cold initial process opens excluded from retained samples and reported separately. No motion or hardware performance claim.

fileOwnershipBenchmark.exploratoryRunConditions: Overlapped the product build/typecheck; retained for provenance, not the primary controlled measurement.

limitations: This implements the file-ownership portion of L1, not the complete L1-L4 restart batch. runProductHost still closes/rebuilds the server, authorization/database and native upload/metadata layer.
Legacy one-shot loadNativeProductMachineProfile retains its existing ownership; process retention requires the new factory or explicit borrowed file resources. Wrappers must forward factory.close.
The file benchmark measures reacquisition/catalog/release only; it does not include metadata layer initialization, MCU configuration or whole printer restart.
The 40 samples per mode on a cached desktop filesystem do not establish target-device tails or printer throughput.
One compiled API-load case passes the existing regression gates; no Python/target-board performance comparison or strict no-regression claim.
No physical stop, numerical anomaly closure, real-client standard restart or full Python retirement was established.
